recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce the exact 2015 last-resort sentence unless OO reopens the later FHIR-10436 status wording, because the current definition is later applied wording and still prevents use of `unknown` as a generic `other` status.
issue_request: FHIR-5669 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request from DSTU1 asking to add `unknown` to the `http://hl7.org/fhir/observation-status` value set with cautionary wording that `unknown` should be a value of last resort.
initial_application: The historical Observation spreadsheet was updated in commit 301f09fdfe86f6fb8da27fe96a5580edfe7bdd0d, whose subject included `[#5669]`; that source added the `unknown` code and the requested last-resort note to the Observation status terminology row.
additional_context: FHIR-10436 later aligned Observation and DiagnosticReport status definitions and rewrote the `unknown` display/definition to the current authoring-system-does-not-know wording, including the caution that it is not an `other` code. Later Observation status issues FHIR-39062 and FHIR-46579 touch status handling but do not remove `unknown` or require a new Observation status code-system/value-set change for this seed.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active Observation resource remains in build scope, `Observation.status` is required-bound to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/observation-status`, that value set includes the `http://hl7.org/fhir/observation-status` code system, and the code system contains `unknown` with cautionary semantics consistent with the later status-alignment wording.

Concluded that a proposed `cannot-be-obtained` status should not update Observation.status, preserving the current status code set.
